classification.difficultyReason: The Cartesian trajectory is given. The student differentiates at x=0 for the angle, solves y=0 for the range, and sets dy/dx=0 then substitutes for the greatest height. These are three direct, signposted applications of standard methods, with no reframing and no representation change. The demand is the same as p45-q2.

content.prompt: A projectile from the origin follows $y=\frac34x-\frac{1}{160}x^2$. Find the angle of projection to 1 decimal place, the range and the greatest height.

answer.short: Angle of projection $36.9^\circ$ above the horizontal; range $120$ units; greatest height $22.5$ units.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac34-\frac{x}{80}\\\tan\theta&=\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=0}=\frac34\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34\right)\approx36.9^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle of projection is $36.9^\circ$ above the horizontal.

For the range, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac34x-\frac{x^2}{160}&=0\\x\left(\frac34-\frac{x}{160}\right)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }120\end{aligned}$$
The range is $120$ units.

At the greatest height, $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac34-\frac{x}{80}&=0\\x&=60\\y(60)&=\frac34(60)-\frac{60^2}{160}\\&=22.5\end{aligned}$$
The greatest height is $22.5$ units.
